cross_item_rule: One construction held across all 24 and is why nothing eliminates: every option in an item repeats the stem's clause verbatim and varies a SINGLE axis (which gap, which surface, which confound, which object of 'two reasons to...'). No lone absolute among hedges, no lone long option, no frame-breaker, no option performing a rhetorical act the others do not - fired 0 times in 24. The only recurring pull was solver-side and did not license any rejection: (a) knowledge of the field's standard true claim (items 1, 3, 7, 16), and (b) a prior that these authors key the measurement/confound option in alternative-explanation menus (5, 9, 13, 22). Both are guesses about authoring habit, not eliminations - I could not defend either to someone holding the passage.

shared_frames.frame: Paired-text 'how would Text 2 respond/agree' items whose options are all menus of alternative explanations for one reported effect (confound / co-intervention / pre-trend / measurement artifact / mechanism). Solving one does not give the answer to another, but the SET teaches which confound type this batch tends to key; if the key is the measurement-artifact option in most of them, that is a cross-item tell worth a with-passage check on 9, 13 and 22 together.

'Function of the last/second sentence' items, each with a fixed lead clause and a varied object. Item 4 is a strict 2x2 and item 10 a strict 'two reasons to X' quartet - the tightest anti-elimination construction in the batch.
'Overall structure' items built as a shared three-beat spine with only the final beat varying. Same authoring template; none leaks.
Word-completion items: four single adjectives, no shared morphology or field, nothing to eliminate on.
Vocab-in-context items: four genuine senses of a common polysemous word. Item 12's 'prosperity' is the only option a test-wise solver would shade down, and that is a habit prior, not a rejection.
